import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Melt the data to create separate rows for each product type and customer
customer_segments_pivot = pd.melt(customer_segments, id_vars=['ID', 'Year_Birth', 'Education', 'Marital_Status', 'Income', 'Kidhome', 'Teenhome', 'Dt_Customer', 'Recency'], 
                                  value_vars=['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'],

customer_segments_pivot = customer_segments_pivot[customer_segments_pivot['Spending'] > 0]

# Plot the data using a violin plot

sns.violinplot(x='Product', y='Spending', data=customer_segments_pivot)

plt.xlabel('Product Type')

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import pandas as pd

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Melt the data to create separate rows for each product type and customer
customer_segments_pivot = pd.melt(customer_segments, id_vars=['ID', 'Year_Birth', 'Education', 'Marital_Status', 'Income', 'Kidhome', 'Teenhome', 'Dt_Customer', 'Recency'], 
                                  value_vars=['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'], 
                                  var_name='Product', value_name='Spending')

# Filter out customers with no spending on any product
customer_segments_pivot = customer_segments_pivot[customer_segments_pivot['Spending'] > 0]

# Plot the data using a violin plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.violinplot(x='Product', y='Spending', data=customer_segments_pivot)
